title: Rational sections of line bundles
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $C$ a smooth connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (an integral scheme by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]) with generic point $\eta$ and function field $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field], and $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Put $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}k(C):=\mathcal L_\eta$, the stalk at $\eta$ [def-sc-rational-section-divisor]. Then $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}k(C)\cong k(C)$ as $k(C)$-vector spaces; in particular $\mathcal L$ has a nonzero rational section $s\in\mathcal L_\eta\setminus\{0\}$ [def-sc-rational-section-divisor]. For every such $s$, with divisor $D=\operatorname{div}(s)\in\operatorname{Div}(C)$ [def-sc-rational-section-divisor] and $\mathcal O_C(D)\subseteq k(C)$ the sub-$\mathcal O_C$-module of the constant sheaf $k(C)$ of [def-sc-divisor], the map

$$
\mathcal O_C(\operatorname{div}s)\longrightarrow\mathcal L,
\qquad f\longmapsto fs,
$$

which sends $f\in\mathcal O_C(D)(U)$, $U$ a nonempty open, to the unique $\sigma\in\mathcal L(U)$ whose germ at $\eta$ is $fs\in\mathcal L_\eta$ (it exists and is unique, see the proof), is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_C$-modules.

proof.text: *$\mathcal L_\eta\cong k(C)$ and $s$ exists.* By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] (1) $C$ is an integral scheme and $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ is a field. By [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk] (1) the stalk $\mathcal L_\eta$ is a free $\mathcal O_{C,\eta}=k(C)$-module of rank one, i.e. $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}k(C)=\mathcal L_\eta\cong k(C)$ (send a basis vector to $1$). Hence $\mathcal L_\eta\neq0$, and any nonzero $s\in\mathcal L_\eta$ is a nonzero rational section in the sense of [def-sc-rational-section-divisor]; $s$ is then a $k(C)$-basis of $\mathcal L_\eta$.

source.place: Tag 02OZ (divisors-lemma-regular-meromorphic-section-exists), proof of case (1): '$\dim_{\kappa(\eta)}\mathcal L_\eta=1$ we can pick a nonzero element $s\in\mathcal L_\eta$'

proof.text: *Local criterion at a closed point.* Fix $s\neq0$ in $\mathcal L_\eta$ and write $D=\operatorname{div}(s)=\sum_Pn_P[P]$ [def-sc-rational-section-divisor]: for each closed point $P$ choose a generator $e_P$ of $\mathcal L_P$ and $g_P\in k(C)^*$ with $s=g_P\lambda_P(e_P)$, so $n_P=v_P(g_P)$ (independent of $e_P$ by [lem-sc-rational-section-order] (1), and $D\in\operatorname{Div}(C)$ by (2) of that lemma). Claim: for $f\in k(C)$, $fs\in\lambda_P(\mathcal L_P)$ if and only if $f=0$ or $v_P(f)+n_P\ge0$. Indeed $fs=(fg_P)\lambda_P(e_P)$, and by [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk] (2) $\lambda_P(\mathcal L_P)=\mathcal O_{C,P}\cdot\lambda_P(e_P)$ with $\lambda_P(e_P)$ a $k(C)$-basis of $\mathcal L_\eta$; so $fs\in\lambda_P(\mathcal L_P)$ iff $fg_P\in\mathcal O_{C,P}$. As $\mathcal O_{C,P}\subseteq k(C)$ is a discrete valuation ring with valuation $v_P$ [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] (3), for $f\neq0$ this holds iff $v_P(fg_P)=v_P(f)+n_P\ge0$, and it holds for $f=0$.

source.place: proof of Tag 0BE8 (divisors-lemma-normal-c1-injective): working locally with $\mathcal L$ trivial, 'Since $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a discrete valuation ring ... the condition signifies that $t\in A_{\mathfrak p}^*$'; here with the generator $e_P$ in place of a trivialization

proof.text: *The sections of $\mathcal O_C(D)$ are the $f$ with $fs\in\mathcal L$.* Let $U\subseteq C$ be a nonempty open and $f\in k(C)$. Every point of $U$ other than $\eta$ is a closed point [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] (2), and $fs\in\mathcal L_\eta=\lambda_\eta(\mathcal L_\eta)$ always. Hence, by [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk] (3), $fs$ lies in the image of the injective map $\lambda_U:\mathcal L(U)\to\mathcal L_\eta$ iff $fs\in\lambda_P(\mathcal L_P)$ for every closed $P\in U$, iff (step 2) $f=0$ or $v_P(f)+n_P\ge0$ for every closed $P\in U$, iff $f\in\mathcal O_C(D)(U)$ by the definition of $\mathcal O_C(D)$ in [def-sc-divisor]. So $\varphi_U(f):=\lambda_U^{-1}(fs)$ is a well-defined map $\mathcal O_C(D)(U)\to\mathcal L(U)$; put $\varphi_\emptyset=0$ (both modules are $0$ over $\emptyset$).

source.place: Tag 01X5 (divisors-lemma-meromorphic-functions-integral-scheme) (2): $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is the constant sheaf $\mathcal L_\eta$, so a meromorphic section $fs$ is a section of $\mathcal L$ over $U$ iff it is so at every point of $U$

proof.text: *$\varphi$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_C$-modules.* $\varphi_U$ is additive since $\lambda_U$ is. For opens $\emptyset\neq V\subseteq U$, the restriction $\mathcal O_C(D)(U)\to\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$ is the inclusion of subsets of $k(C)$ [def-sc-divisor], and $(\sigma|_V)_\eta=\sigma_\eta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; so $\varphi_U(f)|_V$ and $\varphi_V(f)$ both have germ $fs$ at $\eta$ and are equal by injectivity of $\lambda_V$. For $a\in\mathcal O_C(U)$, $a$ acts on $\mathcal O_C(D)(U)$ by multiplication by its germ $a_\eta\in k(C)$ [def-sc-divisor], and $(a\sigma)_\eta=a_\eta\sigma_\eta$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; so $\varphi_U(af)$ and $a\varphi_U(f)$ both have germ $a_\eta fs$ and are equal. Restriction to $\emptyset$ is compatible trivially.

source.place: Tag 01X5 (2): the inclusion $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear

proof.text: *$\varphi$ is an isomorphism.* It suffices that every $\varphi_U$ is bijective (the inverse maps then form an inverse morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_C$-modules); for $U=\emptyset$ this is clear. Let $U\neq\emptyset$. Injective: $\varphi_U(f)=0$ gives $fs=\lambda_U(0)=0$ in $\mathcal L_\eta$, so $f=0$, as $s\neq0$ in the $k(C)$-vector space $\mathcal L_\eta$ (step 1). Surjective: let $\sigma\in\mathcal L(U)$; since $s$ is a $k(C)$-basis of $\mathcal L_\eta$ (step 1) there is $f\in k(C)$ with $\sigma_\eta=fs$. Then $fs$ lies in the image of $\lambda_U$, so $f\in\mathcal O_C(D)(U)$ by step 3, and $\varphi_U(f)=\sigma$ because both have germ $fs$ at $\eta$ and $\lambda_U$ is injective [lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk] (3). Hence $f\mapsto fs$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_C(\operatorname{div}s)\to\mathcal L$.

split_report.summary: Statement corrected and made self-contained: 'integral curve over $k$' replaced by 'smooth connected curve over an algebraically closed field' (def-sc-curves), because for a non-normal integral curve the claim is false (cusp: see the report) and because def-sc-divisor, which defines $\mathcal O_C(D)$, exists only in that setting; both citers (lem-sc-divisor-class-curve, lem-sc-negative-degree-no-sections) use it only there. $\mathcal L\otimes k(C)$ is defined as the stalk $\mathcal L_\eta$, and the map $f\mapsto fs$ is spelled out. The one-paragraph proof became five steps: existence of $s$ (Stacks 02OZ), the local criterion at a closed point (DVR), the description of $\mathcal O_C(D)(U)$ as $\{f: fs\in\mathcal L(U)\}$ through the embedding of $\mathcal L$ in its generic stalk, $\mathcal O_C$-linearity, bijectivity on every open. New nodes: lem-sc-invertible-module-generic-stalk (Stacks 01X5 (2) for invertible modules), lem-sc-rational-section-order (well-definedness and finiteness of orders, Stacks 02SF context and 02SG), def-sc-rational-section-divisor (rational sections, $\operatorname{ord}_P$, $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)$; Stacks 02SF, 0BE6). The blueprint-uses def-sc-curves is now a statement dependency. The Lean of slopmaster2 (exists_tensorObj_dual_toModules_iso, exists_isInvertible_zeroLocus_tensorObj_dual) proves a different statement ($\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O(D_2)\cong\mathcal O(D_1)$ on smooth proper curves, through $\chi$ and twists by ample divisors) and was not followed; its open declarations are not used by this proof.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes the first sentence of the blueprint proof ('$\mathcal L_\eta$ is a free $k(C)$-module of rank one ... a nonzero element $s$ exists'); steps 2-3 realize 'the submodule $\mathcal O_C(D)\subseteq k(C)$ of [def-sc-divisor] is exactly the set of $f\in k(C)$ with $fs\in\mathcal L$' (via '$\mathcal O_C(D)|_U=s^{-1}\mathcal O_U$ by the definition of $D=\operatorname{div}(s)$', here stalkwise at each closed point with a generator $e_P$ instead of a trivialization on $U$); steps 4-5 realize '$f\mapsto fs$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_C(D)\to\mathcal L$'. The phrase 'Writing $D=\operatorname{div}(s)$ for the divisor of zeros and poles of $s$' is def-sc-rational-section-divisor with lem-sc-rational-section-order.
